reason: Functional: the catalog mega menu toggle. The button already displays "Explore", the aria-label restates it, and the chevron inside is aria-hidden with no alternative text of its own. Same template as fi-2296 and fi-2452.

Not functional: a photograph of the CDC campus used as a card image. The alt describes what the picture shows, which is the right thing to do for an informative image, but the link's purpose lives in its title attribute instead.

Functional, and the label is good, but this is the same live call to action as fi-8098, which is already kept. Identical href and identical aria-label on another page of the same site, differing only in the icon's colour class.
Not functional: a story photograph in a headline link, with the headline repeated as its alt. Fifth page of this template on lithub.com, after fi-10373, fi-10425, fi-10448 and fi-10493.

Functional: a puzzle-piece icon linking to the extensions manual. The only text is MediaWiki's default title attribute, "Special:MyLanguage/Manual:Extensions", which is a system path with two namespace prefixes rather than anything written for a person to hear.

Functional, and the alt is good: an icon-only search submit button labelled with its action. Dropped as the third copy of this template, after fi-2297 which is kept and fi-2453 which was dropped for the same reason.

Not functional: a thumbnail of the adult immunisation schedule linking to the easy-read version of the same schedule. The alt is the graphic's title, so a person gets the name of the chart and none of the chart. Same shape as fi-2750.
Not functional: a book cover in a headline link, with the story title repeated as its alt and again as the link's title attribute.
Functional: a link to the full episode. The link carries its own text "Full Episode", the play glyph is a sprite reference with no alternative text, and the thumbnail image has none either.
Functional: a plug icon linking to the API documentation, named only by MediaWiki's default title, "Special:MyLanguage/API:Main page". Same finding as fi-11304 on the same site.

Not functional: a news photograph in a story card. The alt names the person in the picture accurately, but it is also the link's only accessible name, so the link announces a man's name while the article is about approving a stadium club name.
Functional: the universal header logo links to the bureau's own home page. The alt is the bare agency name, which a person already on census.gov knows, rather than the fact that the link goes home.

Not functional: a warning icon inline in the FAQ text. MediaWiki wraps every image in a link to its own file description page, so the interactive ancestor is an artefact of the platform rather than a control anyone authored. The alt conveys the icon's meaning, which is correct for an informative glyph.

Not functional: an award badge used as a story card image. The alt names the badge, including the vendor in brackets, while the headline sits in the link's title attribute where it is announced second at best. Same defect as fi-11276.

Not functional: a campus photograph in a lightbox gallery. The control is the link, which carries its own screen-reader text "Click to expand this slide", and the photograph's short alt plus its figcaption are the right treatment for a content image.
Functional: a teaser link to a press release. The link's own text is the headline and the whole blurb, and the image beside it carries no alternative text at all, so there is no pair to confirm.

Not functional: a news photograph in a story card. The alt is a full caption with a photographer credit, and because it is also the link's accessible name a person hears the caption instead of the headline, which is sitting in the link's title attribute.

Not functional: a news photograph in a story card. The empty alt is correct, because the caption inside the link already carries the headline, and this is the redundancy filter applied the right way round.

Functional: an icon-only footer link to the bureau's account on X. The title names the destination service, including the old name a person may still recognise, and nothing in it describes the glyph. Same pattern as fi-10291.

Functional: a menu item leading to the reviews section. The link's own text reads "Reviews" and the chevron beside it is titled "Chevron", which names the drawing and adds a word a person has to discard.
Not functional: a news photograph in a story card with a correct empty alt. Same template as fi-2141 on the same page.

Functional: shares the current page to X. The aria-label says "Share on Twitter", which names the action, and that matters here because the same site's footer has a visually identical icon that goes to the bureau's own account. The title, "X (Twitter)", would not have distinguished them.

Functional: a role=button that opens the video in a modal. The label names the action and which video it plays, the still behind it is aria-hidden, and the play glyph is too, so there is one unambiguous reference.
Functional: a teaser link to a blog post, with the headline and blurb as the link's own text and no alternative text on the image. Same template as fi-4883.

Functional, and the label is good, the same play-video template as fi-2157 which is already kept. Dropped as a duplicate: identical markup and identical label pattern, differing only in which video it opens.

Functional and informative at once: a fire potential map linking to the outlooks that explain it. The alt names the map and then says "Click for", which is a mouse instruction rather than alternative text, and nothing conveys what the map currently shows.
Functional, and the label is good, but this is the third copy of the play-video template after fi-2157 and fi-2162. Dropped as a duplicate.

Functional: a link to today's fire weather outlook. The visible text says "Today's SPC Outlook" and the image's alt says "SPC Fire Day 1", an internal product code, so a person hears the same thing twice, once in jargon.

Not functional: a news thumbnail in a headline link. The alt describes the rendering of the galaxy rather than repeating the headline, which is a careful piece of informative alt text on an image that is not a control.
Functional: a safety topic link with an icon above its own label. The visible text reads "Heat" and the alt reads "Heat", so the correct alt is empty and the image announces the word a second time.
